items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Bobby was engaged to play the Strand, so he hired Frank Newton and a trombone player named Jonas Walker. That augmented the band to 9 pieces...

ctx.x: After a few months with Johnny Monnegue I left and went to another dancing school and worked with a leader named Bobby Neal. Bobby was a little fellow about 4 feet tall who played a double-B tuba which was the biggest tuba made. It was much easier playing a dancing school job with Bobby than it was with Monnegue because we played many numbers that we did not have to read. And Bobby would do a little show by walking through his tuba and twirling it around the floor. In the band was Arthur Bowie, a pianist, John…

Bobby was working in a small dancing school on the east side of town, but a big school opened on Broadway over the Strand Theater and was called the Strand Ballroom. Bobby was engaged to play the Strand, so he hired Frank Newton and a trombone player named Jonas Walker. That augmented the band to 9 pieces and this job became the easiest dancing school job in New York because another band was also engaged.

It was a high place with plenty of space on the stage for two orchestras and they employed 50 hostesses whereas most places had no more than 15. With 3 brass and 3 saxes we were able to play some special arrangements which were numbered from C-one up to C 15, and one was an arrangement by Benny Carter on Rhapsody in Blue which had been one of the special arrangements played by the Scott band when we started playing other than head arrangements.
